The 2026-2027 call opened on 15 November 2025 and closed on 15 December 2025.

new_scholarship.name: Presidential West African Scholarship Initiative (PWASI) - Government of Ghana for ECOWAS Member States
new_scholarship.funding_type: Government scholarship (benefits not itemised in the official notice)
new_scholarship.official_source: Ghana Scholarships Authority, Government of Ghana
new_scholarship.duration: Up to 4 years undergraduate, 2 years master's, 4 years PhD
new_scholarship.deadline: 30 August 2026 for ECOWAS member states to return the National Endorsement Form
new_scholarship.application_period: The 2026 initiative was published on 3 June 2026. Applicants first apply to a participating Ghanaian public tertiary institution (institution windows from January to September 2026), then submit credentials through the Ghana Scholarships Authority portal, and their home country nominates them, with the National Endorsement Form due to Ghana by 30 August 2026.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Citizens of ECOWAS member states other than Ghana who have applied for admission to a participating Ghanaian public tertiary institution and who meet that institution's admission requirements.
eligibility: Be a citizen of an ECOWAS member state other than Ghana
Meet the admission requirements of the listed participating universities
Demonstrate academic excellence and leadership potential
Demonstrate commitment to contributing to national or regional development
Meet immigration and visa requirements for international students studying in Ghana
requirements: Proof of application to a participating Ghanaian public tertiary institution, either a conditional admission letter or an acknowledgement notice with the application fee paid
Academic credentials and admission letters submitted through the Ghana Scholarships Authority online portal
Nomination by the applicant's national nominating agency in their ECOWAS member state
National Endorsement Form submitted by the nominating agency through Ghana's Ministry of Foreign Affairs
required_documents: Conditional offer letter or application acknowledgement notice
Supporting documents uploaded to the Ghana Scholarships Authority portal
National Endorsement Form (completed by the nominating agency)
application_method: Apply directly to a participating Ghanaian public tertiary institution using that institution's admission link
Submit credentials, admission letters and supporting documents via the Ghana Scholarships Authority online portal
Await shortlisting, then nomination by the nominating agency in your ECOWAS member state
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Selection runs through national nomination: the Ghana Scholarships Authority shortlists and forwards to each applicant's national nominating agency, which nominates up to the country quota. Each of the 14 ECOWAS member states has a quota of 3, for 42 nominees in total.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Students from Benin, Burkina Faso, Cabo Verde, Cote d'Ivoire, The Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone or Togo seeking a fully on-campus degree at a Ghanaian public university.
new_scholarship.notes: Awards are limited to 42 places in total (3 per ECOWAS member state), and the distribution between undergraduate and postgraduate levels is decided by each nominating agency. Priority fields are aligned to ECOWAS regional development priorities, including AfCFTA-related studies.

programme_detail_official.description: The Presidential West African Scholarship Initiative is a Government of Ghana scholarship awarding places to citizens of ECOWAS member states other than Ghana for full-time, on-campus undergraduate and postgraduate study at public tertiary institutions in Ghana. Applicants apply to a participating Ghanaian university and submit credentials through the Ghana Scholarships Authority portal; their home country then nominates them against a quota. The 2026 initiative reserved 42 places in total, three for each of the 14 eligible ECOWAS states.
programme_detail_official.coverage: West Africa: Benin, Burkina Faso, Cabo Verde, Cote d'Ivoire, The Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone and Togo

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you hold citizenship of one of the 14 eligible ECOWAS member states other than Ghana
Pick a participating Ghanaian public tertiary institution from the notice's list and apply within that institution's own admission window
Keep the conditional admission letter, or the acknowledgement notice showing the application fee paid
Upload academic credentials and admission letters through the Ghana Scholarships Authority portal
Identify the designated nominating agency in your own country, because your government must nominate you
Track your country's quota, which is 3 places
common_rejection_risks: Missing your home country's nomination step, which cannot be substituted by a direct application
Not having applied to a participating Ghanaian public institution before submitting to the Authority
Incomplete supporting documents, which the notice says will not be considered
Applying from outside ECOWAS, or applying to Ghana itself
Missing the national endorsement deadline in your own country, which is set earlier than Ghana's
estimated_uncovered_costs: The notice does not itemise what the scholarship pays, so tuition, accommodation, stipend, travel and visa costs cannot be assumed to be covered
Applicants must budget for their own travel to Ghana and for any costs outside whatever their nominated institution later confirms
document_audit: Conditional offer letter from the chosen Ghanaian university, or the application acknowledgement notice
Supporting documents for the Ghana Scholarships Authority portal upload
National Endorsement Form, completed by the nominating agency, not by the applicant

alerts.message: This is not a direct application scheme. Your ECOWAS member state's nominating agency must submit the National Endorsement Form to Ghana through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, so start that process early.
Only 3 nominees per ECOWAS member state, 42 in total, and the split between undergraduate and postgraduate places is decided nationally.
Participating universities publish different application windows between January and September 2026, so the university deadline can bind before the scholarship deadline.

submission_workflow: Choose a participating Ghanaian public tertiary institution from the notice
Apply for admission directly through that institution's portal
Obtain a conditional offer letter or the application acknowledgement notice
Submit credentials and documents through the Ghana Scholarships Authority portal
Contact the nominating agency in your own ECOWAS member state and supply them with your file
Wait for Ghana's shortlisting, national nomination and final award

programme_detail_official.description: The Agence universitaire de la Francophonie, through its Institut de la Formation a Distance de la Francophonie (IFIC), calls each year for applications to its catalogue of more than 150 international distance degree programmes, from licence to doctorat, delivered by more than 45 member institutions in 13 countries. The AUF supports francophone students with a virtual international mobility allowance paid as partial reimbursement of enrolment fees for the most deserving students or those with limited resources, mentoring from application to diploma including the organisation of exams and thesis defences, and free access to AUF offices worldwide during the process. The 2026/27 call ran from 7 April to 14 September 2026, with intake deadlines of 9 June 2026 and 14 September 2026.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Francophonie network: Africa dominates the AUF membership, alongside the Arab Maghreb, Europe and Asia-Pacific. Eligibility is linguistic and network-based rather than nationality-based.

application_readiness_checklist: Choose one of the more than 150 distance programmes in the AUF catalogue at https://l.auf.org/FOAD-FD
Check the start date of that programme, because there are two different intake deadlines
Create an account on the AUF calls-for-applications platform and submit before the matching deadline
Prepare evidence of academic merit or of limited resources, which is what the funding is targeted at
Plan for the fact that only part of the enrolment fees are reimbursed
Email foad@auf.org if anything about the call is ambiguous
common_rejection_risks: Missing the intake deadline that matches the programme start date
Applying to a programme that is not in the AUF distance catalogue
Expecting full funding: only part of the enrolment fees are covered
Failing the entry requirements of the delivering institution
estimated_uncovered_costs: The majority of enrolment fees, because the award is explicitly a partial reimbursement
Living costs, books, materials, internet and examination travel, none of which are mentioned
Travel and accommodation, because the programmes are designed to be studied from home
document_audit: The call page does not itemise documents
Admission documents required by the chosen AUF member institution
Evidence of merit or of limited resources, as the target of the funding

alerts.message: The 9 June 2026 deadline applied to programmes starting in September or October 2026, and the 14 September 2026 deadline to programmes starting in January or February 2027. Check the start date of your chosen programme before picking a date.
The award is described as a partial reimbursement of enrolment fees, so budget for the rest of the tuition.
The call closes at 23:59 Europe/Paris, which is 22:59 UTC in summer and 23:59 UTC in winter. Do not assume your local midnight.

submission_workflow: Browse the AUF distance degree catalogue and choose a programme
Confirm the programme start date and the matching application deadline
Create an account on the AUF calls-for-applications platform
Submit the application with academic and financial supporting evidence
Follow up with foad@auf.org and complete admission at the delivering institution
Track the course, exams and thesis defence with AUF/IFIC support
